latest_messages.headline: Midday: steady, no changes -- both our stocks are up nicely and we're slightly ahead for the day.
latest_messages.body: A quiet, do-nothing check -- exactly right on a calm day. I confirmed both our holdings, JPMorgan (a big bank) and Deere (the tractor/farm-equipment maker), are healthy and gaining, and made sure their automatic safety-nets are still in place. No buying, no selling. The morning's weak-jobs rally kept going, so the whole market drifted higher into midday -- good for the two stocks we own, but it also means the names on my shopping list got MORE expensive, not cheaper, so none met my bar to buy. I'd rather sit patiently in cash than chase a stock higher just because the market's green; discipline on the buy side is how we avoid overpaying. Both positions crossed comfortably into profit, so their trailing stops (an auto-sell that follows the price up and locks in gains if the stock later drops 10%) are doing their job -- protecting the profit we've built. Nothing needs doing until the market-close check this afternoon, when I'll send the full end-of-day scorecard. Next real event I'm watching is the Aug 12 US-China tariff deadline. Equity ~$101,843, up +$308 (+0.30%) today, +1.84% since our $100k start. JPMorgan +$955 (+8.5%), Deere +$808 (+6.2%) -- both green, safety-nets resting below. ~$75,894 cash (~75%) still on the bench, ready for a real bargain.

latest_messages.headline: Open: no trades -- the big jobs report came in weak, stocks jumped, and nothing went on sale. We're up a touch and both holdings are green.
latest_messages.body: Nothing to trade -- and today that's the win. The July jobs report ('NFP') landed just before the open and was surprisingly WEAK: the economy actually LOST 23,000 jobs when Wall Street expected it to ADD about 80,000. Here's the counter-intuitive lesson: a weak jobs report often pushes stocks UP, not down -- softer hiring makes the Federal Reserve less likely to raise interest rates, and cheaper money is good for stocks, so the whole market rallied on the 'bad' news. My pre-market plan was 'if a good stock goes on SALE after the number, we pounce.' But a rally is the opposite of a sale -- my top ideas (Eaton, Quanta, Caterpillar) got MORE expensive, not cheaper. Chasing a name higher just because everything's green is the undisciplined move that costs money, so I stayed put and re-checked my whole list -- nothing cleared my quality bar. I'll keep our ~75% cash ready for any quality name that pulls back to a sensible price. Next event on my radar is the Aug 12 US-China tariff deadline. Equity ~$101,622, up +$88 (+0.09%) so far today, +1.62% since our $100k start. JPMorgan +7.8%, Deere +5.1% (Deere just crossed into +5% territory) -- both green, both on trailing-stop safety-nets. ~$75,900 cash (~75%), three of five slots open, 0 of 3 weekly buys used.

latest_messages.headline: Pre-market plan: staying patient on purpose -- today is the big monthly jobs report, so we keep our cash dry until the dust settles.
latest_messages.body: Research only, market closed. My four research assistants swept overnight news, today's earnings, our two holdings, and fresh buy ideas -- and found nothing to buy and nothing to sell. Two reasons to sit tight: (1) the July jobs report ('NFP' -- how many people got hired last month) lands at 7:30 our time, before the open, and it's a single number that can jolt everything up or down, so buying right into it is a coin-flip we skip; (2) Wall Street now sees roughly an 82% chance the Federal Reserve RAISES interest rates in September to cool inflation, up from ~52% a month ago (a mild plus for our bank, JPMorgan, a mild drag on our tractor-maker, Deere, but nothing that breaks why we own them). And nothing on my buy list is a clean 'yes': my hottest name, Eaton, has run up ~24% in a week and is too overheated to chase; my favorite, Quanta (a power-grid builder), still hasn't broken above its trend line the way I need to see. When nothing clears my quality bar, cash is the smart position. I'll re-check at the open once the jobs number is out -- if it puts a good stock on sale, we have plenty of cash ready, and both holdings stay protected by their trailing-stop safety-nets. Equity ~$101,551 (+1.55% since our $100k start). JPMorgan +8.2%, Deere +4.2%, both green and protected. ~$75,900 cash (~75%), three of five slots open, 0 of 3 weekly buys used.

My watchlist's hottest name (Eaton) is still overheated after a big run; my favorite (Quanta, a power-grid builder) is still sitting on its trend line, not a clean 'buy.' Patience is the position.
